stem: Which three parts make up the recordanelle fusion protein?
choices: A nuclear localization signal, a reverse transcriptase and a DNA-binding domain
A mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein
A mitochondrial membrane anchor, a ribonuclease and a 5′-cap-binding protein
A plasma membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a tRNA synthetase
answer: A mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein
label: Abstract · recordanelle architecture

stem: Up to what fraction of all endogenous mRNAs could the engineered recordanelle sample?
choices: Up to 64%
Up to 15%
Up to 90%
Up to 40%
answer: Up to 90%
label: Abstract · transcriptome coverage

stem: What limitation do the authors give for DNA-based molecular recording methods that encode transient information into DNA?
choices: They need the cells to be fixed before readout
They cannot be read out by sequencing at all
They record only while the cell is not dividing
Mostly confined to prokaryotes or a few target genes
answer: Mostly confined to prokaryotes or a few target genes
label: Introduction · limits of DNA recording

stem: Which RNA-binding domains did the authors first use to test specific RNA recruitment, and what do they bind?
choices: MCP and PCP, binding ms2 and pp7 stem loops
EIF4E and PARN, binding the 5′ cap
PABPC1 and PABPC4, binding the poly(A) tail
LARP1 and LARP4A, binding the poly(A) tail
answer: MCP and PCP, binding ms2 and pp7 stem loops
label: Results · phage RBDs

stem: What served as the mitochondrial anchor in the recordanelle constructs?
choices: The full-length human TOM20 protein
The first 70 amino acids of human TOM20
The transmembrane domain of human AIF
A mitochondrial targeting peptide from yeast Pab1
answer: The first 70 amino acids of human TOM20
label: Results · mitochondrial anchor

stem: In the FISH experiments, where did mCherry RNA carrying pp7 stem loops localize?
choices: Only within MCP-containing recordanelles
Within both MCP- and PCP-containing recordanelles
Only within PCP-containing recordanelles
Diffusely in the cytoplasm, outside any recordanelle
answer: Only within PCP-containing recordanelles
label: Results · specific recruitment by FISH

stem: By qPCR of the mitochondrial fraction, over what range were ms2-tagged mCherry RNAs enriched relative to a mock control?
choices: 1.2-fold to 6-fold
up to 15-fold
20-fold to 50-fold
3-fold to 11-fold
answer: 3-fold to 11-fold
label: Results · enrichment by qPCR

stem: What range of selectivity, measured as the ratio of ms2-tagged to pp7-tagged reporter mRNA, did the MCP-based recordanelles show?
choices: 1.2-fold to 6-fold
3-fold to 11-fold
up to 15-fold
0.1-fold to 0.5-fold
answer: 1.2-fold to 6-fold
label: Results · selectivity ratio

stem: Why did EWSR1- and FUSQG-based constructs bind RNA even with no RNA-binding domain fused to them?
choices: The mitochondrial anchor itself binds RNA nonspecifically
Those full-length assemblers carry RNA-binding domains of their own
The condensates trapped RNA by size exclusion alone
Residual MCP from earlier transfections stayed bound
answer: Those full-length assemblers carry RNA-binding domains of their own
label: Results · nonspecific binding by assemblers

stem: Which assembler peptides showed no nonspecific RNA binding in the absence of an RNA-binding domain?
choices: EWSR1 and FUSQG, which are full-length proteins
G3BP1 and FUS6D, which carry NTF2 domains
TAF15N and FUSN, which are intrinsically disordered regions only
DDX4C and TDP43C, which are full-length proteins
answer: TAF15N and FUSN, which are intrinsically disordered regions only
label: Results · clean assemblers

stem: What happened to which reporter RNA was enriched when the recordanelle's RNA-binding domain was changed from MCP to PCP?
choices: Enrichment stayed with the ms2-tagged reporter
Both reporters became equally enriched
Neither reporter was enriched any more
Enrichment switched to the pp7-tagged reporter
answer: Enrichment switched to the pp7-tagged reporter
label: Results · RBD sets the target

stem: In the RNA-seq comparison against an RBD-less control, what did the full-cell transcriptome of cells with MCP- or PCP-based recordanelles show?
choices: No differentially expressed genes
Hundreds of differentially expressed genes
Depletion of the targeted reporter only
A broad upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes
answer: No differentially expressed genes
label: Results · no transcriptome perturbation

stem: Inside the recordanelle fraction, how did the targeted reporter RNA rank among significantly enriched genes for the PCP-based construct?
choices: It was one of several hundred enriched genes
It was the only significantly enriched gene
It ranked below an enriched predicted lncRNA
It was enriched only after spike-in normalization
answer: It was the only significantly enriched gene
label: Results · specificity by RNA-seq

stem: Why was TAF15N fixed as the assembler while the mRNA-binding domains were varied?
choices: It gave the strongest specific enrichment of any assembler tested
It was the only assembler that localized to mitochondria
It enriched RNA moderately and showed no nonspecific binding on its own
It was the smallest assembler, easing transfection
answer: It enriched RNA moderately and showed no nonspecific binding on its own
label: Results · why TAF15N as baseline

stem: Which of the mRNA-binding recordanelle constructs failed to localize to the mitochondrial membrane?
choices: PABPC4
LARP1
EIF4E
PABPN1
answer: PABPN1
label: Results · localization screen

stem: Up to what fold enrichment did the best generalized mRNA binders, based on LARP1/4A and PABPC1/4, recruit mRNA into the mitochondrial fraction?
choices: Up to 15-fold
Up to 6-fold
Up to 90-fold
Up to 2-fold
answer: Up to 15-fold
label: Results · generalized recruitment efficiency

stem: Which assembler performed best for stem-loop-specific recruitment, and which for generalized mRNA recruitment?
choices: TAF15N for stem-loop-specific, FUSQG for generalized
FUSQG for stem-loop-specific, TAF15N for generalized
FUSQG was best for both kinds of recruitment
TAF15N was best for both kinds of recruitment
answer: FUSQG for stem-loop-specific, TAF15N for generalized
label: Results · assembler depends on RBD

stem: Why did the bulk RNA-seq characterization of generalized recruitment add synthetic RNA spike-ins?
choices: To measure the per-sample sequencing error rate
To calibrate the efficiency of mitochondrial fractionation
Much of the transcriptome binds, so global quantification needs them
To tell which captured transcripts were nuclear in origin
answer: Much of the transcriptome binds, so global quantification needs them
label: Results · spike-in normalization

stem: What proportions of genes expressed in HEK293T cells were enriched in the FUSQG- and TAF15N-based recordanelles against a nonbinding control?
label: Results · transcriptome-scale enrichment

stem: What do the authors clarify that the 64-90% enrichment figures mean?
choices: That share of transcript species is represented in the organelle
That share of all RNA molecules in the cell is bound
That share of recordanelles hold at least one mRNA
That share of the cells carry a working recordanelle
answer: That share of transcript species is represented in the organelle
label: Results · what the percentage means

stem: Which transcripts were discordant between the recordanelle fraction and the whole cell?
choices: Interferon-stimulated genes and other stress transcripts
Nuclear transcripts such as Xist, and mitochondrial RNAs
Highly expressed housekeeping mRNAs
Short-lived transcription factor mRNAs
answer: Nuclear transcripts such as Xist, and mitochondrial RNAs
label: Results · concordance with the cytoplasm

stem: In the doxycycline reporter cell line, how quickly did induced mCherry::ms2 mRNA fall back to baseline without a recordanelle?
choices: Within about 2 hours
Within about 5 days
Within about 1 day
It never returned to baseline
answer: Within about 1 day
label: Results · reporter decay window

stem: What transcript recovery ratio did recordanelles built with PCP, MCP, LARP1 or LARP4A give at the full-cell level?
choices: Around 0.7, well above the mock control
Around 2, well above the mock control
Around 0.5, about half the mock control
Around 0.07, similar to the mock control
answer: Around 0.07, similar to the mock control
label: Results · constructs that did not protect

stem: How much higher was transcript recovery after 1 day for the PABPC1/4-based recordanelles?
choices: 2-4-fold higher
10-15-fold higher
About 1.1-fold higher
About 90-fold higher
answer: 2-4-fold higher
label: Results · protection by PABPC1/4

stem: What surprised the authors about recordanelles built with MCP, LARP1 or LARP4A?
choices: They protected RNA but did not recruit it
They recruited RNA but did not protect it
They failed to reach the mitochondrial surface
They protected RNA only in dividing cells
answer: They recruited RNA but did not protect it
label: Results · recruitment is not protection

stem: What explanation do the authors offer for poly(A)-binding recordanelles protecting RNA better than MCP-based ones?
choices: PABPC4 proteins bind more copies of each transcript than MCP
MCP-based condensates are less dense than PABPC4-based ones
PABPC4 proteins bind the poly(A) tail directly, while MCP binds upstream of it
PABPC4 proteins recruit deadenylase inhibitors to the organelle
answer: PABPC4 proteins bind the poly(A) tail directly, while MCP binds upstream of it
label: Results · why the poly(A) tail matters

stem: Two days after doxycycline removal, where was mCherry::ms2 significantly protected in recordanelleV1- and V2-expressing cells?
choices: At the mitochondrial level only
At the full cell level only
At neither level, once the control was matched
At both the full cell and the mitochondrial level
answer: At both the full cell and the mitochondrial level
label: Results · two-day protection

stem: Why did the authors judge recordanelleV2 superior to recordanelleV1 in the doxycycline experiment?
choices: It recorded the transient RNA without changing its initial expression level
It recorded the transient RNA for more days after removal
It localized to mitochondria more faithfully
It recruited a larger share of the transcriptome
answer: It recorded the transient RNA without changing its initial expression level
label: Results · V2 over V1

stem: Which two interferon-stimulated genes did the authors track by qPCR in the IFNB recording experiments?
choices: OAS3 and IFIT3
IFIT1 and IFI44L
IFI6 and IRF9
RIGI and ISG15
answer: IFIT1 and IFI44L
label: Results · ISG readouts

stem: Two days after IFNB removal, what had become of the interferon-stimulated gene signal in control recordanelleMCP cells?
choices: It was reduced but still clearly detectable
It had increased above the day-0 level
It had decayed to be indistinguishable from never-stimulated cells
It persisted in the mitochondrial fraction only
answer: It had decayed to be indistinguishable from never-stimulated cells
label: Results · control signal decay

stem: What did the authors observe for interferon-stimulated gene detection in recordanelleV1 cells between day 0 and day 2 after IFNB removal?
choices: It fell by roughly half while staying detectable
It stayed exactly level with day 0
It increased for the housekeeping gene as well
It sometimes increased rather than merely being maintained
answer: It sometimes increased rather than merely being maintained
label: Results · V1 signal amplification

stem: In passaged cells, how long after stimulus removal could recordanelles still capture interferon-stimulated genes?
choices: 3-4 days, with the signal lost from day 5
5-6 days, with the signal lost from day 7
1-2 days, with the signal lost from day 3
Indefinitely, with no measured loss
answer: 3-4 days, with the signal lost from day 5
label: Results · recording duration with passaging

stem: What do the authors conclude explains the shorter recording window in passaged cells?
choices: Nucleases degrade the condensate over time
Cell division and growth dilute the recorded transcripts
Mitochondrial turnover destroys the anchor
The assembler peptide dissociates as it is diluted
answer: Cell division and growth dilute the recorded transcripts
label: Results · why the record fades

stem: Which two genes remained differentially expressed in control cells 2 days after IFNB removal?
choices: IFIT1 and IFI44L
OAS3 and IFIT3
IFI6 and IRF9
RIGI and ISG15
answer: IFI6 and IRF9
label: Results · genes the control retained

stem: What recall of the day-0 differentially expressed genes did recordanelleV2 achieve 2 days after IFNB removal?
choices: About 90%
About 64%
About 50%
label: Results · DEG recall

stem: What did Gene Ontology analysis of the genes retained by recordanelleV2 in the mitochondrial fraction show?
choices: A detailed picture of the past IFNB response
Only interferon-independent stress pathways, not ISGs
Mitochondrial respiration terms, not immune ones
No enriched biological process above background
answer: A detailed picture of the past IFNB response
label: Results · reconstructing the response

stem: What happens to general mRNA recording when the TAF15N assembler is removed from recordanelleV2?
choices: It is unchanged, since the RBD does all the work
It is diminished, though specific recruitment survives
It is abolished, specific recruitment included
It improves, since nothing excludes transcripts now
answer: It is diminished, though specific recruitment survives
label: Results · the assembler is needed

stem: In the quantitative proteomics 2 days after IFNB removal, how did recordanelleV2 cells compare with recordanelleMCP controls?
choices: Interferon-stimulated proteins stayed elevated in recordanelleV2 cells
Mitochondrial respiratory chain proteins were depleted in recordanelleV2 cells
They were indistinguishable, with all but RIGI and ISG15 back to baseline
Every interferon-stimulated protein had returned to baseline in both
answer: They were indistinguishable, with all but RIGI and ISG15 back to baseline
label: Results · no extended inflammatory state

stem: What did assays of ATP production, apoptosis, membrane potential and aerobic metabolism show for recordanelle-expressing cells?
choices: Less ATP made
More apoptosis
Lower potential
No substantial change
answer: No substantial change
label: Results · mitochondrial function

stem: What did dimensionality reduction of the single-cell RNA-seq data reveal about cluster 6?
choices: It appeared only in IFNB-stimulated cells
It appeared in unstimulated cells too
It appeared in control cells only
It appeared only after 5 days
answer: It appeared only in IFNB-stimulated cells
label: Results · the IFNB response cluster

stem: Two days after transient IFNB treatment, which construct still had a substantial proportion of cells in the IFNB response cluster?
choices: recordanelleMCP only
recordanelleV2 only
Both constructs, at similar proportions
Neither construct, once construct-specific clusters were excluded
answer: recordanelleV2 only
label: Results · single-cell recording

stem: Using the ISG gene-activity module, what happened to the day-0 signature of stimulated recordanelleMCP cells by day 2?
choices: It was retained
It doubled
It disappeared
It moved cluster
answer: It disappeared
label: Results · ISG module over time

stem: Which perturbations do the authors say a transcriptional recorder imposes on cells by its very nature?
choices: Depolarized mitochondria, apoptosis, loss of aerobic metabolism, cell death
Sustained interferon signaling, excess protein translation, prolonged inflammation
Blocked nuclear RNA export, ribosome sequestration, stalled translation
Transgene burden, membrane occupancy, RNA depletion, storage costs
answer: Transgene burden, membrane occupancy, RNA depletion, storage costs
label: Discussion · intrinsic perturbations

stem: How does the recordanelle differ in principle from prior molecular recording strategies?
choices: It stores unmodified molecules in a protective compartment
It encodes the information into DNA instead of RNA
It modifies RNA chemically instead of storing it
It samples at fixed intervals instead of continuously
answer: It stores unmodified molecules in a protective compartment
label: Discussion · what is different

stem: How large is the single protein a recordanelle requires, which the authors note is small enough for common viral vectors?
choices: About 25 kDa, from 0.7 kb of coding sequence
About 91 kDa, from 2.5 kb of coding sequence
About 180 kDa, from 5 kb of coding sequence
About 300 kDa, from 8 kb of coding sequence
answer: About 91 kDa, from 2.5 kb of coding sequence
label: Discussion · size and deliverability

stem: Which alternative use of the recordanelle do the authors propose as a live-cell substitute for methods like RIP-seq and CLIP-seq?
choices: Measuring mitochondrial membrane potential
Mapping the half-life of individual transcripts
Profiling the specificity of an RNA-binding domain
Tracing cell lineage through sequential barcodes
answer: Profiling the specificity of an RNA-binding domain
label: Discussion · RBD profiling

stem: What application do the authors suggest for recordanelleV1, given that it appears to let recorded RNAs be translated?
choices: Recording for longer periods than recordanelleV2
Recording without any effect on the transcriptome
Profiling the specificity of RNA-binding domains
Artificially sustaining and amplifying an intracellular signal
answer: Artificially sustaining and amplifying an intracellular signal
label: Discussion · V1 as an amplifier

stem: How do the authors contrast recordanelles with the concurrently introduced TimeVault tool?
choices: Free-floating particles for 24-hour snapshots, against anchored continuous recording
Anchored continuous recording, against free-floating 24-hour snapshots
Recording into DNA, against recording of unmodified RNA
Recording in prokaryotes only, against recording in human cells
answer: Free-floating particles for 24-hour snapshots, against anchored continuous recording
label: Discussion · comparison with TimeVault
